title: Row ids
summary: Entity rows are keyed by TypeIDs that every device agrees on.

requirements.text: Every entity table (one with a prefix in `ID_PREFIXES`) is keyed by a TypeID: its prefix and a UUID, `meal_01jd4x8m2kf7r9q3vz5w6t0hyc`.

history.text: Every table's key is a TypeID string, the table's prefix and a UUIDv7 (`meal_01jd4x8m2kf7r9q3vz5w6t0hyc`), never an auto-increment integer.
history.reason: Version 1 didn't match the product: settings, per-day and sync tables use natural keys, and derived ids are UUIDv8.

history.text: Every entity table (one with a prefix in `ID_PREFIXES`) is keyed by a TypeID: its prefix and a UUID, `meal_01jd4x8m2kf7r9q3vz5w6t0hyc`; other tables use a natural key, and none uses an auto-increment integer.
history.reason: Version 2 held two promises; the other tables' keys is now ID-5.

requirements.text: Tables without a prefix use a natural key, and no table uses an auto-increment integer.
A table's prefix never changes once rows exist.
A row imported from an external system gets an id derived from the table and its external key, so two devices importing it agree on the id.
The TypeScript and Rust id encoders and the SQL id migration are tested against the TypeID specification's examples.

history.text: The TypeScript, Kotlin and Rust id encoders produce the same ids, pinned to the TypeID specification's examples.
history.reason: Version 1 didn't match the product: the Kotlin encoder has no such test.
